The fit is reported for roughly 30-220 MPa; 181.4 MPa is inside it. Bending loss: Woodhouse and Lynch-Aird, Acta Acustica 105 (2019) 517-, Sec. 3 and Eq. 16 text: nylon E = E' + iE'' with E'' = 0.25 GPa independent of stress and frequency in the kHz range (eta_E = E''/E' about 0.04 to 0.02). The shared material owner takes a Kelvin-Voigt bending viscosity, whose loss factor grows with frequency, so it is set to E''/(2 pi 2000 Hz) = 19894 Pa s: exact at 2 kHz, low below and high above (a documented model-form gap; hysteretic loss would be constant). Its effect on mode n is lambda eta_E with lambda about B n^2, so the lowest partials are essentially unaffected; air drag is the cylinder-gas-loading record
